name: volume_profile_breakout_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Price consolidates at high-volume nodes (HVN) where many participants have transacted. When price breaks away from an HVN with above-average volume, trapped traders (who bought/sold at the HVN) are forced to exit, creating follow-through. The inefficiency exists because HVN/LVN analysis requires real-time volume profiling which most retail participants don't compute. Not arbitraged because volume profile is noisy intraday and identifying true breakouts vs false ones requires additional filters.

indicators.name: poc
indicators.formula: price level with highest cumulative volume today (Point of Control)

indicators.name: value_area_high
indicators.formula: upper bound of 70% volume distribution (VA High)

indicators.name: value_area_low
indicators.formula: lower bound of 70% volume distribution (VA Low)

long.confirmation: close above value_area_high for 2 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: close below value_area_low for 2 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market on second confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: poc (for longs) or poc (for shorts) — i.e., back into value area
exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-enters value area and holds for 5 bars

filters.time_filter: no entry in first 30 min (let profile develop) or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer breakouts in direction of index trend (nifty EMA(21) slope)
other_filters: skip if value area width > 2x ATR(20) daily — range too wide

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — microstructure edge, decays as more participants use volume profile

weaknesses: Volume profile is computationally intensive to update in real-time and the POC/VA boundaries shift throughout the day, creating moving targets.
Early in the session (<30 min), the profile is unreliable — insufficient data. Waiting for 30+ min of data means missing morning breakouts.
False breakouts from value area are common — 55-60% of breakouts reverse. The volume confirmation helps but doesn't solve the problem entirely.
prior_art: Market Profile / Volume Profile analysis. James Dalton's 'Markets in Profile'. TPO-based analysis adapted to volume-at-price.
notes: Consider using prior day's volume profile (POC, VAH, VAL) as reference levels instead of building intraday — more stable reference points.
